name: Per-Gaussian Backward Pass
definition: A backward pass optimization that parallelizes over Gaussians instead of pixels to reduce the number of required atomic operations by a factor equal to the number of pixels in each tile (256 for 16x16 tiles).
summary: The Per-Gaussian Backward Pass is a parallelization strategy that accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting training by computing gradients per Gaussian instead of per pixel, reducing atomic contention at the cost of higher VRAM usage.
